title: Flow cytometry assay and cell staining protocol
author: Miloje Savic

steps_raw.instruction: Flow cytometry assay and cell staining protocol
Miloje Savic and Jennifer L. Dembinski
Infection Control and Environmental Health, Norwegian Institute of Public Health, Oslo, Norway

This protocol describes antigen stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), staining for various surface and intracellular molecular markers, followed by flow cytometry measurements. PBMC contain various T and NK cell populations, which produce cytokines upon specific stimulation with antigens. T (and NK) cells can be stimulated in various ways: using whole virus, bacteria (or membrane fractions of bacterial lysates), antigenic peptides etc. The stimulation guide provided with this protocol refers to stimulation with antigenic peptides, influenza virus and a standard cell mitogen (Concanavalin A, ConA), though it can be adapted to incorporate any other cell stimulant.

This method is used to stimulate influenza specific cytokine production. After PBMC stimulation, cells are stained to detect cytokine producing T (and/or NK) cells by flow cytometry. Antigens are presented by antigen presenting cells (APC), which are also present among PBMC. In this procedure the Golgi apparatus is blocked by Brefeldin A and Monensin in order to keep all the cytokines produced after stimulation within the cell. The number of influenza specific cytokine producing T (and/or NK) cells can be determined by staining cells with fluorophore conjugated antibodies specific for the cytokine(s) of interest and counted on a flow cytometer.
Thaw PBMCs and overnight rest
Follow the Thaw procedure from the ‘Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) and plasma isolation from whole peripheral blood’ protocol.
Resuspend cells in complete media: RPMI 1640 with 10% (heat inactivated) FBS and pen/strep antibiotics added. Ideally, cell concentration should be 2-5 million cells/ml in 50ml tube.
Incubate cells overnight at 37°C (~18h) with loose caps in humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Wash PBMC from previous night, resuspend in complete media, and re-count.
A minimum cell viability of 66% is required for use in ICS assays1
Prepare Activation medium containing GolgiPlug, CD28 and CD49d as described in Table 1.
Adjust final cell count in Activation medium at 5 million live cells/ml
Plate in U-bottom 96 well plates 200µl/well of cell suspension (in this way each well will have 1 million live cells)

Important: Each experimental condition should have at minimum 1 million live cells stimulated and measured in flow cytometry. If sample availability is restrictive, DMSO blank and ConA samples can be reduced to 0.5 million cells each.
For each PBMC sample prepare in Activation medium (Table 1):
DMSO blank control (final concentration should match concentration in antigen peptides)
ConA control (at 5µg/ml final concentration per well)
CD4 peptide library (at 4µg/ml final concentration per well)
CD8 peptide library (at 4µg/ml final concentration per well)
Influenza H2O2 inactivated2 virus (75 HAI unites per well)

For peptide libraries (and DMSO blank control): in general, dilute peptides (resuspended in 100% DMSO) in media and DMSO to ensure that the final concentration of each peptide in the master mix will provide a 4µg/ml final concentration and an equal percentage of DMSO among libraries and the control in the experimental wells.
Add 20µl of the appropriate stimulation to each well
Incubate at 37°C in humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 4-6 hours
Table 1. Activation medium.
Cell fixation and staining
Wash cells 2 times with 200µl of (cold) FM (350 x g, 5 min, 4oC).

If using LIVE/DEAD stain – stain with 0.5µl in 100µl PBS per well, 30 min 4°C. In parallel, stain the ArC compensation beads (in a tube) one drop solution A with either 3µl live/dead (Aqua) or 1µl (IR))
Wash 1x with FM media (or PBS) (use 3ml FM for ArC beads in tube)
Resuspend ArC beads in 500µl FM and add one drop solution B to tube. The beads are now ready for flow cytometry, keep them at 4°C protected from light. Do not fix these beads!
Add 100 µl of cold Fix/Perm solution to wells with cells, mix and incubate (20 min, 4oC, dark) (vortex while adding to prevent clumping of cells).
Wash cells 2 times by re-suspending the cells in 200 l PW (add 100 l PW to cells in Fix/Perm solution for first wash).
In parallel, add 2 drops of negative and 2 drops of positive BD compensation beads in each bead well to stain for single color compensations and spin down with second PW cell wash step
Note: depending on the antibody origin (mouse and/or rat) used for staining, adequate anti-mouse and/or anti-rat Ig, κ/Negative Control Compensation Particles Set has to be used.
Now, in parallel, prepare compensations (Ab compensation beads) as described below.
If using more than one BD Horizon Brilliant™ Violet colored antibody add 50µl Brilliant stain buffer per well (add to the 6 color master mix and add 150µl/well for those wells)
Add 100 µl PW solution containing fluorophore-conjugated antibodies (see below).
Incubate plate (30 min, 4°C, dark)
Add 100 µl PW and spin (350 x g, 5 min).
Wash 2 times with Perm/Wash solution (350 x g, 5 min).
Re-suspend the cells in 250 µl FM and run them on flow cytometer after compensating, or store cells overnight at 4°C in the dark and run flow assay the next morning.
Compensations Ab beads only procedure:
Bead wells – make one well per antibody by using 2 drops of negative and 2 drops of positive beads
Add 100µl per bead well of single antibody in PW: 5µl or 20µl antibody stock solution in 95 or 80 µl of PW depending on antibody test size (see manufacturer instruction)
Stain same as rest of plate – follow all steps as staining the cells
Important: The samples can be stored protected from light for maximum 72 hours at 4°C (no more than 24 hours is preferred).
Flow cytometry measurements
Acquire at least 40,000 CD4+ T cells (or 20,000 CD3-CD7+ NK cells).
Table 2. Lymphocytes medium (LM) (RPMI 10% (heat inactivated) FBS, 1% PS).
Table 3. Flow Medium (FM).
Table 4. Perm Wash solution (PW): PW is a 10x solution – needs to be diluted in milliQ H2O before use.
Take one tube from -20°C, defrost and add 50µl DMSO.
Add 0.5µl of LIVE/DEAD stain per 100µl PBS per well.
Add 1µl IR per 1 drop ArC beads or 3µl Aqua per 1 drop ArC beads.
LIVE/DEAD stain can be stored for 8 weeks at -20°C.
